BKS1.claim: Kasol is a hamlet in the Parvati Valley between Bhuntar and Manikaran — 30 km from Bhuntar, 3.5 km from Manikaran and 36 km from Kullu.

evidence.quote: It is situated in Parvati Valley , on the banks of the Parvati River between Bhuntar and Manikaran .
It is located 30 km (19 mi) from Bhuntar , 3.5 km from Manikaran and 36 km (22 mi) from Kullu town

BKS2.claim: Kasol is popular with backpackers and is the base for treks to Malana and Kheerganga.

evidence.quote: Kasol is a popular Himalayan destination for backpackers and acts as a base for nearby treks to Malana and Kheerganga .
Elevation 1,580 m (5,180 ft)

BKS5.claim: Kasol has no rail or air link of its own; it is reached by road.

evidence.quote: Kasol is only connected to the rest of India by well-developed roads.

KA1.claim: Kasol is nicknamed 'Mini Israel': many Israeli travellers come after military service, and cafés serve Israeli food with Hebrew menus.

evidence.quote: Kasol has drawn foreign backpackers for decades, especially Israeli travellers who come after their compulsory military service.
its cafés serve Israeli food and print menus in Hebrew

KA2.claim: Manikaran is a Hindu and Sikh pilgrimage town; its hot spring, inside the Manikaran Sahib Gurudwara, is hot enough to cook rice, and the gurudwara serves langar.

evidence.quote: It is a pilgrimage centre for both Hindus and Sikhs and the hot spring inside the Manikaran Sahib Gurudwara is considered auspicious.
is so hot that rice can be cooked in it
Traditional feeding (Langar) of visitors at Manikaran

KA3.claim: For Kheerganga, ride to Barshaini and walk 11 km; the hot spring is accessible from end-April to end-October, and there is no electricity at the top.

evidence.quote: you first need to take a local bus or a motorcycle till Barshaini
it is an 11-km walk till Kheer Ganga
which is accessible from the end of April to the end of October every year
Carry a torch, as there is no electricity in Kheer Ganga.

KA4.claim: End-April to end-October suits treks and camping; late December to February brings snow.

evidence.quote: End-April to end-October. In the other months, stay at Kasol is possible but the snow and temperature will make it tough to trek and camp
receives a fair amount of snowfall from late December to February

KA5.claim: Travellers also stay in Tosh, Kalga, Pulga and Chalal; Tosh is cheaper than Kasol.

evidence.quote: who also stay in nearby villages such as Tosh, Kalga, Pulga and Chalal
Tosh is less expensive than its neighbour town Kasol.

KA6.claim: Malana, on a side valley, governs itself through a council tied to its deity Jamlu; an 1871 report noted its people kept apart from outsiders.

evidence.quote: Malana governs itself through a village council linked to its deity, Jamlu
recorded that the villagers of Malana kept apart from their neighbours, did not eat or marry outside the village

KA7.claim: A number of foreign tourists have gone missing in and around the valley since the early 1990s.

evidence.quote: A number of foreign tourists have gone missing in and around the valley since the early 1990s.

KA8.claim: Cannabis is illegal in India under the NDPS Act, 1985, with narrow exceptions such as bhang.

evidence.quote: Cannabis remains illegal in India under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, with certain exceptions for medical use, scientific research, and traditional preparations like bhang.

KA9.claim: Kasol is about 534 km north of Delhi; from Bhuntar turn off for Kasol via Jari.

evidence.quote: 534 km N of Delhi
From Bhuntar (before Kullu), take the right turn to Kasol via Jari.

KA10.claim: A trek from Kasol to Grahan village runs through forest with waterfalls.

evidence.quote: This trek starts from Kasol and is composed of six villages Grahan, Padri, Ratapani, Nagaru, Biskeri and Bhandak Thatch.
The path leads through a lush green forest, with beautiful waterfalls on the way.

KA11.claim: The Parvati rises at the Mantalai Glacier; its water is freezing even in early summer.

evidence.quote: The Parvati River begins at the Mantalai Glacier within the Parvati Valley.
The waters can be freezing even during the early summer

overview.text:
Kasol is a riverside hamlet in the Parvati Valley, 30 km from Bhuntar and 3.5 km from Manikaran, at about 1,580 m. Backpackers have come for decades — so many from Israel that it is nicknamed 'Mini Israel', with Hebrew menus in its cafés — and it is the base for treks to Kheerganga's hot spring, Grahan and Malana, and for stays in Tosh, Kalga, Pulga and Chalal.

Manikaran, a Hindu and Sikh pilgrimage town with a hot spring hot enough to cook rice, is just up the road. Kasol has no rail or air link; it is reached by road from Bhuntar via Jari. End-April to end-October suits trekking; late December to February brings snow. Treat the valley with care: cannabis is illegal under the NDPS Act, and foreign trekkers have gone missing here since the 1990s.
